item.title: White House Whipsaws Silicon Valley (and Itself) Over A.I. Rules
item.description: The Trump administration has struggled over how to approach to “open source” models, which are freely available to download and favored by Chinese companies.
item.dc:creator: David McCabe, Mike Isaac, Ana Swanson and Kate Conger
item.media:description: Chinese open-source artificial models like Kimi, made by Moonshot AI, have added a new and urgent dimension to the fight between Washington and Beijing over who will control critical technologies.

item.title: Pirro Meets With Trump at the White House After He Said She ‘Choked’ in Reflecting Pool Case
item.description: President Trump said Jeanine Pirro, the U.S. attorney for Washington, D.C., “folded like an umbrella.” For now, her job appeared to be safe, according to two people familiar with the meeting.
item.dc:creator: Erica L. Green, Katie Rogers, Tyler Pager and Maggie Haberman
item.media:description: President Trump on Monday in the Oval Office, where he grew angry when asked whether he had spoken with Jeanine Pirro about her decision to withdraw a felony charge against a former Olympic canoeist.

item.title: Spotlight on Fauci Said to Boost Book Sales for Kennedy and His Publisher
item.description: Health Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., his son, and Senator Rand Paul have all written books criticizing Dr. Anthony S. Fauci. All were published by a company led by a close Kennedy adviser.
item.dc:creator: Sheryl Gay Stolberg
item.media:description: Robert F. Kennedy Jr., now the health secretary, published “The Real Anthony Fauci” in 2021.

item.title: Ronald Lauder, a Billionaire G.O.P. Backer, Closes His Wallet
item.description: Ronald S. Lauder, a major funder of conservative political causes, has not given a single dollar this year to Republicans in his home state, and his super PAC has gone idle.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Fandos
item.media:credit: Krista Schlueter for The New York Times
item.media:description: Ronald S. Lauder, at a Frick Collection dinner in 2021, has so curtailed his political donations that no Republican in New York has received any money from him this year.

item.title: Trump, Graham Dominate Senate Race: 5 Takeaways from South Carolina Debate.
item.description: The legacy of Lindsey Graham loomed over the field to replace him in a debate Monday. All eyes were on his sister, Darline, who was endorsed by President Trump.
item.dc:creator: Patricia Mazzei

item.title: How the War in Iran Is Complicating Trump’s Agenda at Home
item.description: As President Trump heads to the West Coast to talk to Americans about the economy, the war in Iran is driving up costs and polls show the already unpopular conflict is losing support.
item.dc:creator: Erica L. Green
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Pete Marovich for The New York Times
item.media:description: President Trump has been the only president in the modern era to take the country to war without the support of the American public.

item.title: Sailors Working in Strait of Hormuz Are Caught in Crossfire of Iran War
item.description: Thousands of civilian workers remain stranded on ships at risk of attack by Iran. On one vessel, sailors have been held by the Iranian navy for more than three months.
item.dc:creator: Jenny Gross and Peter Eavis
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:credit: Tomas Munita for The New York Times
item.media:description: U.S.-Israel attacks against Iran on Feb. 28 followed by Iran’s almost-immediate closure of the Strait of Hormuz, has stranded thousands of sailors.

item.title: An Emerging Deal Between Iran and Oman to Reopen Hormuz Would Come at a Cost for Trump
item.description: The deal would address President Trump’s most urgent political problem by allowing ships to move again. But it would give Iran strategic leverage it did not have before the war.
item.dc:creator: David E. Sanger, Farnaz Fassihi and Eric Schmitt
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
United States Defense and Military Forces
item.media:description: Ships in the Strait of Hormuz seen from Musandam, Oman, in June. An emerging deal, if it happens, would reopen shipping traffic in the strait, according to Iranian and U.S. officials.

item.title: Saudi Aramco Reports 33% Profit Surge Despite War’s Disruption
item.description: Higher oil prices propelled a quarterly earnings jump for Saudi Arabia’s energy giant, which used pipelines to work around disruptions in the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Lisa Friedman
item.category: US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)

item.title: A Currency Trader at Heart, Bessent Bets on Japan’s Yen
item.description: Coordinated intervention allowed Japan to support its currency without selling off its U.S. debt holdings.
item.dc:creator: Alan Rappeport
item.media:credit: Tierney L. Cross for The New York Times
item.media:description: Scott Bessent, the Treasury secretary, last week returned to his roots as a hedge fund manager in making a currency bet to help stabilize Japan’s currency.

item.title: Uber’s Strategy for Fighting Sexual Assault Suits: ‘What Were You Wearing?’
item.description: The ride-hailing giant promised to handle legal claims “in a way that is best for the survivor.” Its lawyers are pursuing a far more aggressive strategy.
item.dc:creator: Emily Steel

item.title: Cambridge Professor’s Jason Arday’s Work Challenged Ahead of Book Launch
item.description: A knife-wielding masked man. A pig’s head outside his parents’ door. Running 30 marathons in 35 days. The Cambridge professor Jason Arday, accused of plagiarism, says he’s been through it all. Not everyone believes him.
item.dc:creator: Jennifer Schuessler and Alexandra Alter
item.media:credit: via Simon & Schuster; Photo by Anselm Ebulue

item.title: Using a Gun to Defend Yourself? The Right to Kill Is Growing.
item.description: States are pushing to pass laws sanctioning more reasons to use lethal violence in self-defense, a distinctly American tradition.
item.dc:creator: Mike McIntire

item.title: After Deadly E-Bike Crashes, N.Y. Lawmakers Consider Crackdown
item.description: The City Council on Tuesday is expected to present 17 proposals to make electric bikes and scooters safer for riders and pedestrians.
item.dc:creator: Stefanos Chen
item.media:credit: Graham Dickie for The New York Times
item.media:description: Among the bills under consideration are ones that would ban the sale of some high-speed e-bikes that are currently legal and that would increase penalties for riders who flee the scene of a crash.

item.title: What to Know About Legal and Illegal E-Bikes in New York
item.description: After a series of fatal crashes, often involving illegal devices, officials in New York City are weighing new rules for electric vehicles.
item.dc:creator: Emma G. Fitzsimmons
item.media:description: Several types of electric bikes and scooters are legal in New York City, but many others, including those that can travel at high speeds, are banned.

item.title: Phoenix Species Project Announces Funds for Imperiled Wildlife

item.title: Drone Explodes on Russian Beach, Killing 7, Officials Say
item.description: It was unclear what the drone was targeting and why it crashed in the crowded resort spot, but it has been a deadly summer for civilians caught up in the Russian-Ukrainian war.

item.title: JPMorgan Again Entangled in a Soccer Fiasco
